content:
maya: Heads up — prod-serving pool us-west-2-batch-7 is hitting OOMs since 16:03 UTC. Spike in kv_cache_alloc + kernel mem. Rolling errors: "CUDA out of memory" in allocator.cc:142. Uploading a minidump to the incident snapshot: https://internal/snap/3501236789

infra-bot: Alert — pipeline:oom_rate ↑ 12x; nodes affected: 3/8; incident id INC-3501236789. Autoscaling paused for pool due to frag-level alarms.

simon: On it. Quick mitigation plan: 1) flip runtime circuit breaker to degrade; 2) route heavy requests to a quantized fallback (q4_*); 3) throttle batch size + limit concurrency. Keep changes minimal and reversible.

zara: Agreed. Also: temporarily reduce kernel workspace multiplier to force slim kernels, and evict largest prefixes from KV cache for the most memory-hungry models. That should free transient workspace pressure.

alex: Commands to run (dry-run then apply):
```
# enable degrade circuit
redwoodctl routes update --pool us-west-2-batch-7 --policy degrade
# promote fallback model (no version alias swap until canary verified)
redwoodctl models promote --from model-prod/v2 --to model-prod/q4-fallback
# set batch caps
redwoodctl config set --pool us-west-2-batch-7 batch_max_tokens=1024 batch_size=8
```

simon: Also flip kv cache off for the hot model to avoid large prefix loads:
```
redwoodctl cache set --model model-prod/v2 enabled=false
```

zara: If disabling cache spikes latency too much, do a canary redirect 10% traffic first:
```
redwoodctl traffic split --model model-prod/v2 --model model-prod/q4-fallback 90/10
```

maya: I'm running targeted evictions now for keys with large embeddings and long prefix histories. Starting with model-prod/v2 -> evict top-5 largest prefixes. Will monitor memory and error delta.

ops-oncall: LB throttling applied for pool: inbound reduced by 20% to smooth spikes. Notifying downstream teams about transient SLO impact.

infra-bot: Live profile snapshot available: https://internal/prof/3501236789. Kernel-selection heatmap shows a MATMUL allocation spike during step 3 and workspace high watermark at 87% on affected nodes. Recommend reducing `kselector.workspace_mult`.

simon: Also enable buffer reuse on the runtime to reduce transient allocations: add `--reuse-buffers=1`. That matched staging improvements yesterday (about -18% peak mem).

alex: Temporary runtime patch to apply flags:
```
# apply to pool instances
runtimectl update --pool us-west-2-batch-7 --flag reuse_buffers=on --flag kselector.workspace_mult=0.6
```

zara: If nodes still OOM, fallback path is: route heavy tails to `dedicated-small` pool (prewarmed) and evict remaining KV shards. We'll need to watch tail-latency after that.

maya: Evictions executed. OOM count trending down: 12x -> 1.2x over 4 minutes. Cache remains disabled for a 10min observation window. Telemetry: oom_rate now ~1.1x baseline, workspace highwater dropped to 62%.

simon: Nice. Post-incident follow-ups:
- Add auto-trim policy: when workspace > 75% for >30s, trim KV per-model by LRU until headroom recovered.
- Add runtime metric for buffer reuse effectiveness (mem_saved_per_minute) and a daily job to surface regressions.
- Add a CI canary that simulates KV-heavy prefix sequences to catch regressions in kselector/allocator combos.

maya: Follow-ups assigned: simon -> implement auto-trim policy, zara -> perf test and validate workspace_mult impacts, alex -> open runbook PR and add the runtime flag toggle to emergency playbook. I'll open the incident ticket and link action items.

ops-oncall: Incident created INC-3501236789. Tagging SRE and runtime oncall. Will keep channel updated with metrics. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: Note for postmortem: capture kernel-selection changes in the 24 hours before spike and any recent merges touching allocator.cc, kselector or kv_cache eviction logic.

maya: Thanks team — keeping monitoring up. If OOM rate creeps back up, we revert routing and escalate to infra escalations.
